subject: Chemistry
title: Technetium: The First Artificial Element
description: A 60-second lesson on Technetium: The First Artificial Element.

hook.text: Element 43 was a gap in the table for decades. Every claim of discovery turned out to be wrong.

buildup.text: Mendeleev predicted it. Chemists searched in ores and minerals worldwide. Nothing.

discovery.text: In 1937, Carlo Perrier and Emilio Segrè found it in a discarded piece of a cyclotron from California.

twist.text: They named it technetium—from 'technetos,' Greek for 'artificial.' It was the first element made by humans.

climax.text: Technetium is now used in 30 million medical scans per year. The artificial element saves real lives.

punchline.text: Nature never made it. Humans did. Now it saves millions of lives.

quiz.question: Why is technetium called 'artificial'?
options: It was the first element created by humans, not found in nature
It is made entirely of synthetic polymers
It can only exist in a laboratory vacuum

details.summary: Technetium, created by Carlo Perrier and Emilio Segrè in 1937 by bombarding molybdenum with deuterons, was the first element produced artificially. Its name means artificial from the Greek technetos..
details.whyItMatters: Technetium proved that the periodic table contains elements that must be created artificially. Its isotope technetium-99m is the most widely used radioactive tracer in medical diagnostic imaging worldwide.
takeaways: Technetium was the first element ever produced artificially in a laboratory
No stable isotopes exist, explaining its absence from terrestrial minerals
Technetium-99m is used in over 30 million medical imaging procedures annually

faq.question: Why does technetium not exist naturally on Earth if lighter elements do?
faq.answer: Unlike most elements with atomic numbers below 83, technetium has no stable isotopes. Any technetium created during Earth's formation has long since decayed, with its longest-lived isotope having a half-life of 4.2 million years..

faq.question: Why is technetium-99m so important in medical imaging?
faq.answer: Technetium-99m emits gamma rays at an ideal energy for detection by medical cameras while having a short 6-hour half-life that limits radiation exposure to patients. It can be chemically attached to various molecules that target specific organs..
